rules.statement: An alienation by an executor de son tort for the purpose of paying the debts of the deceased is valid and will pass the property, at any rate so long as the executor de son tort is really acting as executor, and the creditor has reason to believe that he is so acting.
rules.supporting_quote: The lawful acts done by an executor de son tort are good, and an alienation by a person so acting for the purpose of paying the debts of the deceased is valid and will pass the property (see Parker v. Kett [1 Lord Raymond 661. ]), at any rate so long as executor de son tort is really acting as executor, and the creditor has reason to believe he is so acting (Thomson v. Harding[(1853) 2 Ex. B. 630.]).
